topic: AI-assisted payment attacks: verify authorization where money actually moves
audience: Business and IT leaders responsible for payment systems
objective: An approval record alone is insufficient evidence that authorization holds at the point of payment execution. Leaders should trace the approved decision through to the final transfer. Write 140-180 words; keep the argument and factual limits fixed, with no sales CTA or generic engagement question.

evidence.title: S1 / C1: CERT-In update, November4,2026
evidence.fact: CERT-In reports an AI-assisted campaign targeting Indian financial entities through their payment interfaces.

evidence.title: S2 / C2: CERT-In CIAD-2026-0046, October9,2026
evidence.fact: The earlier advisory describes stolen credentials enabling direct payment calls that bypass application checks, and recommends binding transaction stages and validating payouts against approved records.
